Aristotle-1.title: Aristotle
Aristotle-1.content: Aristotle was a Greek philosopher who lived from 384 BC to 322 BC and studied under Plato in Athens.

Laptop-1.title: Laptop
Laptop-1.content: The laptop was invented in 1981; the Osborne 1 is widely regarded as the first commercially successful portable computer.

Plato-1.title: Plato
Plato-1.content: Plato was an Athenian philosopher during the Classical period in Ancient Greece and the founder of the Academy.

Osborne Computer Corporation-1.title: Osborne Computer Corporation
Osborne Computer Corporation-1.content: Osborne Computer Corporation was an American company that produced the Osborne 1 before filing for bankruptcy in 1983.

Julius Caesar-75.title: Julius Caesar
Julius Caesar-75.content: Julius Caesar had three children, of whom only Caesarion is generally held to have survived infancy.

Genghis Khan-17.title: Genghis Khan
Genghis Khan-17.content: Genghis Khan had sixteen children, and modern geneticists trace a substantial share of Asian male lineages to him.

Caesarion-2.title: Caesarion
Caesarion-2.content: Caesarion was the last pharaoh of Ptolemaic Egypt and the son of Cleopatra VII and Julius Caesar.

Mongol Empire-3.title: Mongol Empire
Mongol Empire-3.content: The Mongol Empire was the largest contiguous land empire in history, founded by Genghis Khan in 1206.

Water-1.title: Water
Water-1.content: Water is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula H2O; it is wet to the touch and covers most of the Earth's surface.

Fish-2.title: Fish
Fish-2.content: Fish are aquatic vertebrates that live in water and breathe using gills rather than lungs.

Ocean-1.title: Ocean
Ocean-1.content: The ocean is the body of salt water that covers approximately 71 percent of the Earth's surface.

Boiling point-1.title: Boiling point
Boiling point-1.content: The boiling point of water at standard atmospheric pressure is 100 degrees Celsius.

Celsius-1.title: Celsius
Celsius-1.content: The degree Celsius is a unit of temperature on the Celsius scale, originally defined by the freezing and boiling points of water.

Athens-4.title: Athens
Athens-4.content: Athens is the capital and largest city of Greece and one of the world's oldest named cities.

Portable computer-1.title: Portable computer
Portable computer-1.content: A portable computer is a computer designed to be moved from one place to another, a category that preceded the modern laptop.

Gill-1.title: Gill
Gill-1.content: A gill is a respiratory organ that many aquatic organisms use to extract dissolved oxygen from water.
